comment: The app UI bridge, protocol 2 (epaper-dashboard docs/SLOWBOARD.md §7.7 App UIs). The hub's chrome (crates/slowhub/web/app.js) and the dev chrome (@slowboard/dev) implement every call; @slowboard/app wraps them. A copy lives in epaper-dashboard at crates/slowhub/web/protocol.json; keep the two identical.
negotiation: The handshake still says protocol 1: protocol 1 bundles refuse any other number, and they must keep connecting. An app says the protocol it speaks in connect's argument, {protocol: 2}; the chrome answers connect with `protocol`, the highest both speak (1 from a protocol 1 chrome, which ignores the argument). A protocol 1 app sends no argument and gets protocol 1 behaviour: it never calls the protocol 2 calls and ignores events it doesn't know.

changed.connect: Takes {protocol}; answers with the agreed protocol.
changed.secrets.status: Each entry gains kind (value | oauth), label, help, last_used, and for oauth auth, multiple, scopes, granted_at and accounts [{account, scopes, granted_at, last_used}]. name, optional and set keep their meaning.
changed.secrets.set: A value only: on an oauth secret it fails with code kind.
changed.secrets.clear: A second argument, an account, disconnects that one account of a multiple oauth secret; without it the whole secret is cleared (an oauth secret is disconnected, and revoked at the provider).

2.secrets.connect: secrets.connect(name, {account}?) -> {url}. For an oauth secret: the chrome starts the sign-in at top level itself (the frame never sees the provider's URL, code or state) and answers with url, a link on the hub that starts it again, for a page whose pop-up was blocked. The outcome comes as a secret event. On a value secret it fails with code kind.
2.secret: {event: 'secret', name, ...that secret's status entry}: after a set, clear, connect or disconnect, from this tab or another.
